related_questions.question: What is the AIDS virus?
related_questions.snippet: Overview. Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), is an ongoing, also called chronic, condition. It's caused by the human immunodeficiency virus, also called HIV. HIV damages the immune system so that the body is less able to fight infection and disease.

related_questions.snippet: Key Facts. HIV, the virus that causes AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome), is one of the world's most serious health and development challenges. Approximately 40 million people are currently living with HIV, and tens of millions of people have died of AIDS-related causes since the beginning of the epidemic.

related_questions.question: What is the most common type of AIDS virus?
related_questions.snippet: HIV-1 is the most common type of HIV, and it occurs all over the world. According to the HIV awareness charity Avert, around 95% of people living with HIV have HIV-1. HIV-2 is mainly present in West Africa, but it is slowly starting to appear in other regions, including the United States, Europe, and India.

text_blocks.snippet: The virus that causes AIDS, HIV, is believed to have originated from chimpanzees in Central Africa. It is thought to have jumped from chimpanzees to humans through contact with infected blood, likely during hunting activities. Specifically, the SIVcpz virus (Simian Immunodeficiency Virus) in chimpanzees is closely related to HIV and is believed to be the source of the virus that causes AIDS.
snippet_highlighted_words: believed to have originated from chimpanzees in Central Africa

list.title: SIV to HIV:
list.snippet: Simian Immunodeficiency Virus (SIV) is a virus that naturally infects various primate species, including chimpanzees. It is very similar to HIV, and scientists believe that SIV in chimpanzees (SIVcpz) crossed over to humans and mutated into HIV.

list.title: Cross-species Transmission:
list.snippet: This jump from chimpanzees to humans is called cross-species transmission. It is thought to have occurred through contact with infected chimpanzee blood, possibly during hunting or butchering.

list.title: Initial Spread:
list.snippet: The earliest known case of HIV-1 infection in humans dates back to 1959 in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo. While the virus was circulating at low levels for some time, the AIDS pandemic began to emerge in the 1980s with increased urbanization and travel.

list.title: HIV-1 Group M:
list.snippet: The predominant form of HIV-1 that caused the AIDS pandemic is known as HIV-1 group M. It is believed to have originated in southeastern Cameroon.

list.title: Not Man-made:
list.snippet: It's important to note that there is no evidence to support claims that HIV was man-made or spread through polio vaccination campaigns. The overwhelming scientific evidence points to a natural origin from chimpanzees.
